meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Samoa (International Companies regime, administered by the Samoa International Finance Authority)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (English common law heritage with customary law elements)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the Independent State of Samoa on the Promotion and Protection of Investments (signed 2018)
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations (PACER Plus), in force for Samoa since 2020

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (Act No. 8 of 1987), as amended, ss. 26-27 (registered office), s. 33 (register of members), s. 36 (register of directors); Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2007, as amended; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Regulations 2008; Samoa International Finance Authority Act 2003; FIU Consolidated Beneficial Ownership Guidelines (current edition).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each UBO, director and secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague countries)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (recent utility bill or bank statement dated within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing utility company or licensed bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague countries)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or certificate of incorporation of any corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the corporate UBO's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague countries)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter evidencing lawful source of subscription funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank in the UBO's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague countries)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory electronic screening of all UBOs, directors, officers and authorized signatories against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Samoa domestic sanctions list and the Samoan FIU PEP database. PEPs, their family members and close associates (as defined in the AML/CFT Act 2007) automatically trigger enhanced due diligence, including source-of-wealth verification. Screening is continuous and real-time through registered-agent compliance software; any match or suspicious activity requires a suspicious transaction report (STR) to Samoa's Financial Intelligence Unit within the statutory deadline.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) e-Registry portal for International Companies (https://www.sifa.ws)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered legal name must be in Latin/Roman characters (English). Chinese-character names are not accepted as the statutory registered name; a Chinese-character trade name may be used in parallel after incorporation, provided it is a phonetic or equivalent transliteration of the registered name and is disclosed to the registered agent.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected applicant may extend the reservation (before expiry) by paying the statutory renewal fee to SIFA. Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written appeal with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 days of the notice of refusal, stating the legal basis for acceptance and attaching any ministerial or regulatory consent for sensitive tokens. If the Registrar affirms the refusal, the applicant may apply to the Supreme Court of Samoa for judicial review within 21 days, or re-file under a fresh name with a new reservation fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted. The statutory registered office is the licensed registered agent's address in Apia; no physical or virtual office premises in Samoa are required for a cloud-delivered Micro-SaaS business. The registered agent arrangement fully satisfies the registered-office requirement under the International Companies Act 1987.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 5%). SIFA conducts document-based supervision of licensed registered agents and rarely performs unannounced physical inspections at the premises of non-resident, digitally operated International Companies.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and reservation application fee
International Company incorporation government filing fee (authorized capital up to USD 1,000,000)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: SIFA statutory government fee schedule (tax-exempt regime)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent and registered office service (year 1)
AML/CFT onboarding, UBO register setup, PEP and sanctions screening
Notarization and apostille/consular legalization of UBO identification bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and Ministry of Foreign Affairs (origin country)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Chinese-to-English translation of corporate constitutional documents
Courier delivery of legalized documents to Samoa registered agent

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended — ss. 5–9 (incorporation and constitution), s. 25 (registered office), ss. 27–29 (directors and officers), s. 92 (tax exemption)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form IC-1 (Application for Registration of an International Company) accompanied by the Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; subscription may be nominal and no escrow or capital deposit is required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Company's Application for Registration filed with the Registrar of International Companies is ratified and adopted; RESOLVED FURTHER that the subscriber's share subscription allotment, as recorded in the Register of Members, is approved; RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office shall be at the address provided by the registered agent, who shall file annual returns and maintain corporate records; RESOLVED FURTHER that [Name] is appointed Sole Director, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as President, each to serve until successor appointment; RESOLVED FURTHER that banking arrangements and payment facilitator agreements (Paddle, Lemon Squeezy) are authorized; RESOLVED that the Chairman is authorized to execute all incidental documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance and engagement of licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Services Division, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two to three proposed company names in English (with optional Chinese transliteration) via a SIFA-licensed registered agent; verify against prohibited and reserved name lists; obtain written name clearance before proceeding.
required_dossiers: Certified KYC documents of ultimate beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is refused, the agent re-submits alternative names within 24 hours; no further government fee is charged for re-submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, notarization and execution of constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed registered agent with notary public (Samoa)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association, including Chinese-language counterpart if endorsed by the client; subscriber signs before a notary or in counterparts with notarized signature; registered agent retains original executed set.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (English with optional Chinese annexure)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries a clause, amend and re-execute the relevant article, then re-file; curative process is completed without re-paying the entire fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation application and payment of government fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registry Office, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form IC-1 together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association, consents and the SIFA fee receipt; the registered agent submits electronically or in person at SIFA's Apia registry window.
required_dossiers: Registered agent and registered office consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is requisitioned, the agent supplies the requested information or corrected documents within 14 calendar days; the matter is then prioritized for resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and certifies the statutory registers (members, directors, secretary) upon verification; the company acquires legal personality on the certificate date.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any typographical error in the certificate is cured by applying for rectification under the Act; the Registrar issues a corrected certificate within two business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation governance: first board meeting, share issuance and bank onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the International Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or adopt written minutes passing the pro-forma resolution; issue share certificates, appoint officers, adopt the common seal, and instruct the commercial bank (or qualifying foreign bank) to open the operating account; onboard Paddle and Lemon Squeezy as payment facilitators.
required_dossiers: Minutes of first board meeting (or written resolution)
Register of members and allotment schedule
Bank account opening pack with KYC
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If quorum is unavailable, the written resolution route is used; the chairman certifies the minutes, and non-complying appointments are re-validated by subsequent written resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Annual compliance, tax-exempt status and records maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) and registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain the registered office and agent in Samoa, file the annual return with SIFA, and maintain financial records at the registered office; confirm the statutory tax exemption for international companies and obtain the certificate if required by payment processors or banks.
required_dossiers: Register of directors, members and charges
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filings are cured within a 3-month grace period; penalty relief may be requested in writing to SIFA upon showing reasonable cause.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the entity is a pure cloud software publisher under ISIC 6201; no manufacturing or physical industrial establishment requires a license. If a physical Apia office is later established, Occupational Safety and Health Division, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) would apply.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating or manufacturing permit required; statutory license exemption applies to the Micro-SaaS subscription model. Payment facilitation (Paddle, Lemon Squeezy) does not require a Samoan financial services license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no physical development or emissions; a purely digital software operation does not trigger any EIA category under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, or solid waste thresholds apply; compliance is limited to general electronic-waste disposal under standard environmental good practice if office hardware is used in Samoa.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for a virtual registered office; if a physical workplace is opened in Apia, a fire safety clearance from the National Fire and Emergency Services Authority (NFESA) and a workplace registration with the Occupational Safety and Health Division (MCIL) would be required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (MfR), Samoa, successor agency to the Samoa Revenue Authority; national tax portal: TAXIDENT e-services at https://www.mfrsamoa.ws, covering TIN registration, VAGST returns, income tax and electronic payments; Samoa Customs operates within the MfR for export clearance purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned International Company obtains its statutory TIN through the following SOP: (1) incorporate and register the IC with the Registrar of International and Foreign Companies under the International Companies Act 1987, maintaining a registered office and licensed resident agent in Samoa; (2) submit the prescribed TIN application through the TAXIDENT portal or via a licensed Samoan tax agent, attaching the certified certificate of incorporation, registered office and resident agent confirmations, board resolution authorising the tax representative, and the register of directors and shareholders; (3) file a declaration of offshore business scope to obtain the IC tax exemption certificate, which exempts the entity from income tax and VAGST on all offshore-derived business; (4) apply separately for VAGST registration only where the entity conducts a Samoan taxable activity or exceeds the WST 100,000 taxable-supply threshold, noting that an exempt offshore IC ordinarily remains outside the VAGST registration net; (5) receive the TIN certificate and activated TAXIDENT credentials within 5-10 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa has no US-style check-the-box classification; entity taxation follows the International Companies Act 1987 and the Income Tax Act 2015. Available statutory elections include: (a) an election by an IC to waive its exempt status and be assessed as an ordinary Samoan resident company, applying Samoa's territorial source rules which tax only Samoan-source income; (b) an election to form a VAGST group of related companies where a Samoan taxable activity exists; and (c) elections connected with controlled foreign company attribution where the IC owns reportable foreign interests. No hybrid mismatch election is available. Samoa applies general anti-avoidance and substance-based principles to entities claiming offshore exemption, and for US federal tax purposes the Samoa IC is a non-elective per se corporation that cannot choose pass-through status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax) - Samoa's GST-type value-added consumption tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 annual taxable turnover for mandatory registration; voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold. A Tax_Exempt_Zone International Company with purely offshore SaaS revenue is not a taxable person, and no VAGST registration is triggered.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time e-invoicing or fiscal clearance mandate exists in Samoa. VAGST invoices must contain the statutory content prescribed under the VAGST Act 1998 and be retained for 7 years. Monthly VAGST returns and payments are filed electronically through the MfR TAXIDENT portal, which supports e-filing and e-payment but does not require API-integrated clearance, fiscal digital stamping, or SAF-T bulk reporting.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the VAGST Act 1998, exports of goods and services may be zero-rated at 0%. A Samoan IC supplying micro-SaaS subscriptions to non-resident consumers qualifies where the software or IP is licensed and the digital service is delivered and consumed outside Samoa, the recipient is a non-resident at the time of supply, and no local Samoan supply nexus exists. Where a Merchant of Record such as Paddle or Lemon Squeezy acts as the supplier of record for destination-jurisdiction VAT, the IC's inward settlement payment from the Merchant of Record is treated as export-of-services consideration for Samoan VAGST purposes and may be zero-rated, supported by Merchant of Record settlement reports and subscriber-level sales evidence. The IC must retain proof that no revenue was derived from a Samoan domestic source and must not maintain a taxable presence in Samoa.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic Customs Export Declaration (CED) submitted through Samoa Customs/MfR for any physical goods movement
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or courier receipt evidencing exportation from Samoa
Commercial invoice and signed SaaS subscription/cloud services agreement identifying the non-resident recipient and offshore delivery of the digital services
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement confirming receipt of export consideration in foreign currency into a Samoan licensed bank account
VAGST zero-rating support file including Merchant of Record settlement reports, KYC details of SaaS end-users, IP logs demonstrating offshore consumption, and the IC's tax exemption certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: False export zero-rating or IC-exemption claims expose the entity to: (i) full retrospective clawback of the denied 15% VAGST with a reassessment window of up to 7 years (unlimited in cases of fraud or wilful evasion); (ii) penalty tax of up to 100% of the tax shortfall plus a late-payment surcharge of 5% per month capped at 25%, with interest; (iii) criminal liability for wilful evasion or fraudulent export documentation, carrying fines up to WST 100,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years; and (iv) cancellation of the IC's tax-exemption certificate and compulsory deregistration. The MfR may also apply transfer-pricing and general anti-avoidance rules, and the Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime Act 2007 may attach financial-crime penalties where export documentation is fabricated to conceal undeclared offshore revenue.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), Foreign Exchange Department, operating under the Exchange Control Act 1976 and the Exchange Control Regulations 1977; the offshore/international financial services sector is additionally supervised by the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) operates under a managed-float regime administered by the CBS. Current-account transactions for residents are generally convertible, but capital-account outflows and resident foreign-currency retention require CBS permits or licensed-dealer authorization. A Samoan International Company (IC) is statutorily treated as a non-resident, is prohibited from transacting in Tala with Samoan residents, and executes all treasury activity exclusively in a foreign functional currency (typically USD). Consequently, the IC enjoys full capital-account convertibility for inward shareholder equity or loan injections, and there are no CBS conversion permits or profit-remittance approvals applicable to dividends, director fees, or intercompany settlements originating from the IC's offshore USD accounts. The sole practical remittance hurdles are bank-level AML/beneficial-ownership scrutiny and correspondent-bank compliance, not CBS exchange-control authorization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the CBS Exchange Control Regulations, resident exporters must obtain declared export-license status, repatriate export proceeds to a licensed Samoan bank within the prescribed statutory window (normally ninety days from shipment), and convert a CBS-mandated percentage of the foreign proceeds into WST. A Samoan International Company is wholly exempt from export-proceeds surrender and mandatory conversion ratios because it is a non-resident foreign-currency entity generating SaaS subscription revenue exclusively through offshore Merchant-of-Record platforms (Paddle and Lemon Squeezy); therefore, no repatriation timeline, conversion obligation, or CBS surrender declaration applies to the IC treasury.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Non-resident International Company Operational Account - USD multi-currency (no capital escrow required as minimum capital is nil)
Non-resident International Company Operational Account - USD/GBP/EUR multi-currency suite
Operational Account - onshore retail-commercial focus; International Company non-resident onboarding generally not offered

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low. Samoa has no electronic-money-institution (EMI) or payment-service-provider licensing regime; the CBS does not recognize offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Airwallex, Currenxie, Wise Business) as regulated deposit-taking or clearing institutions within Samoan jurisdiction. A Samoa IC may use a foreign EMI purely as a collection-side account only where the EMI's own jurisdiction and KYC policy accept a Samoa-licensed registered agent, apostilled corporate documents, and non-resident IC beneficial-ownership declarations; however, most global EMIs restrict onboarding for Samoa-domiciled entities or impose enhanced due diligence that materially delays payouts. The prudent blueprint is to use onshore commercial bank USD accounts as the primary treasury spine and permit Paddle/Lemon Squeezy payout settlements directly into those accounts, with no offshore EMI dependency.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Partial remote opening permitted. Samoa's AML/CFT framework (Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 and CBS directives) requires licensed banks to identify all natural-person beneficial owners; however, banks accept remote onboarding where the IC submits notarized or apostilled passport copies of directors and beneficial owners, apostilled Certificate of Incorporation and Register of Directors/Shareholders, a bank-issued professional reference letter, and a live video-identification interview with the compliance officer. In practice, at least one director or authorised signatory is often required to attend a branch interview in Apia to execute the account mandate and specimen signature cards; a Samoa-registered agent acting under a Power of Attorney may complete the physical-execution step for remote shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity arising from nominee directors or layered offshore holding structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully completed CBS/SIFA Beneficial Ownership Declaration identifying all natural persons and their percentage interests; apostilled Register of Directors, Register of Shareholders and Register of Charges; nominee agreement or trust deed if applicable; notarized passports of all signatories and beneficial owners; signed AML questionnaire evidencing source of funds for the initial capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mandatory compliance flag due to beneficial owner or fund-source residence in a high-risk or sanctioned jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written Source of Wealth and Source of Funds statement substantiated by six months of shareholder bank statements; independent tax-residence certificates or tax returns; confirmed economic-nexus letter from the Samoan registered agent; corporate structure chart tracing every intermediate entity; negative-news and PEP screening report from a recognized commercial due-diligence database.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Misclassification of SaaS Merchant-of-Record (MoR) settlement flows as unlicensed money transmission or e-money activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Merchant-of-Record agreement with Paddle or Lemon Squeezy confirming the MoR is the merchant of record and settlement counterparty; platform payout statements and MRR reports; end-customer subscription contracts and software license terms; ISIC 6201 scope declaration; legal opinion confirming the IC is not engaged in money services business under Samoan law because it never holds customer funds and receives only net settlement remittances.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP name-match hits arising from generic name similarity and lack of corporate substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Company-screening and sanctions-clearing report against OFAC, EU, UN, Samoa Consolidated Sanctions lists; resolution of name-match via full corporate identifier (number, date of incorporation, registered agent confirmation); apostilled Certificate of Good Standing from the Samoa Registrar of International Companies; evidence of commercial substance in the form of executed SaaS vendor contracts, cloud-infrastructure invoices, and the registered office agreement in Apia.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol requires the non-resident shareholder to originate a SWIFT MT103 (preferably GPST-tracked) from its home-bank account in the same legal entity name to the Samoa IC's USD operational account at BSP or Pacifika Bank. The wire instruction must carry a coherent purpose code aligned to CBS balance-of-payments classification, e.g., equity investment in an international company, direct investment for share subscription, or intercompany loan. The supporting verification bundle should include the IC board resolution authorizing share allotment or loan drawdown, signed subscription agreement or loan agreement, share register entry, allotment ledger, and a source-of-funds letter from the remitting bank. No CBS approval is required because the IC is non-resident, but the Samoan receiving bank will apply standard AML screening on the remitter, so the remitter's name and country of residence should match the disclosed beneficial-ownership schedule.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: All outbound settlements from the Samoa IC are executed in USD through SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 Cover only for nostro-refinancing) via the Samoan bank's global correspondent network in New York, Sydney, or Suva. For a micro-SaaS treasury, trade-related disbursements consist only of software-vendor payments (cloud hosting, licensing, developer subcontractors), platform fees, legal/accounting retainers, and profit distributions to the shareholder; commercial letter-of-credit rails are not applicable and would generate unnecessary KYC friction for ISIC 6201 digital services. Paddle and Lemon Squeezy settlement inflows arrive as net aggregated USD transfers supported by platform settlement reports; the IC treasury should reconcile each settlement against MoR statements and retain transaction-level export documentation despite the absence of Samoan physical-export formalities.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Offshore USD/WST Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) executed with a global investment bank or licensed broker outside Samoa, permissible for a non-resident IC without CBS registration because the contract settles in USD offshore and does not involve a WST-denominated Samoan resident account.

Cross-currency swap (USD vs WST) under an ISDA Master Agreement with a non-resident counterparty, permissible where no settlement occurs through a Samoan resident bank and the WST leg is deliverable only outside Samoa.

Deliverable USD/WST forward contract with a CBS-licensed dealer is technically permissible for documented commercial exposure but is practically unavailable to International Companies and is not recommended given the IC's non-resident status and statutory prohibition on Tala transactions with Samoan residents; the pragmatic hedge is full USD natural hedging with immediate USD settlement via Paddle/Lemon Squeezy collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary of incorporation; administrative grace period of 30 days is customarily recognized
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of WST 100 (approx. USD 37) per month; continued failure for 3 months triggers administrative strike-off and cessation of corporate existence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Treasury, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Samoa (via registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary date of incorporation; payable simultaneously with the annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest accrues at 1.5% per month on unpaid renewal fees; non-payment for 6 months results in compulsory dissolution and strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent (under Samoa AML/CFT Act and International Companies Act record-keeping obligations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of incorporation; within 14 days of any share transfer, change of controllers, or UBO update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update beneficial ownership records may render the registered agent unable to provide statutory services, lead to an anti-money laundering compliance order, and subject the company to administrative monetary penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No independent statutory audit is required for an ordinary Samoa International Company. Compulsory audit applies only to licensed insurance, banking, or reinsurance entities; a technology micro-SaaS entity is exempt unless its constitution mandates an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) recognized; Samoa local GAAP (Samoa Financial Reporting Standards) also permitted for internal record-keeping. No financial statements are filed publicly or with the tax authority.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must annually confirm the accuracy of the beneficial ownership register for each International Company. Every share transfer or beneficial ownership change must be reported to the registered agent within 14 days for AML/CFT record updating; no public UBO registry filing is made.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficial Owners (held by registered agent)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - USD 1,200 per annum (registered office, registered agent, AML/KYC and formation agent services)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable - no statutory audit required for this qualifying international micro-SaaS company

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% standard corporate income tax (CIT) for resident Samoa companies under the Income Tax Act 2015; 0% headline CIT for an International Company (IC) registered under the International Companies Act 1987, which operates in a statutory tax-exempt zone.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full statutory exemption from CIT, dividend withholding tax, interest withholding tax, and royalty withholding tax for ICs; no capital gains tax; no minimum capital requirement; the annual flat government fee (paid via the registered agent) replaces all profit-based taxation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return (Form AR-IC), filed electronically through the Samoa International Companies Registry e-portal operated by the Ministry for Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL); a tax-exempt IC files no income tax return, but the annual return and annual government fee are mandatory.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 30 calendar days after each anniversary of incorporation; the annual government fee is payable on the same due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company registration number (RC-IC number issued by the Registrar of International Companies).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the RC-IC number exactly as shown on the Certificate of Incorporation; no WST taxpayer number applies to an exempt IC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name and any name change made during the reporting year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the registered English name; a Chinese-language trade name is permissible only if the Registrar approved it as a secondary name.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office in Samoa (physical street address of the licensed IC service provider and registered agent).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm the Samoan registered agent address; a non-resident shareholder may not substitute an overseas address for the Samoan registered office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors: full names, residential addresses, nationalities, passport identification, and dates of appointment or cessation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident and corporate directors are permitted; attach passport or ID copies for the KYC and protective beneficial-ownership file maintained by the registered agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shareholders and beneficial owners: name, address, nationality, class and number of shares, and ultimate beneficial ownership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: 100% non-resident ownership is permissible; the beneficial owner declaration remains confidential but must match the protected register held by the registered agent in Samoa.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorised and issued share capital, currency of denomination, and consideration stated as paid on issued shares.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Shares may be issued in any currency and with any par value; bearer shares are prohibited since the 2014 amendment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory declaration that the IC has not carried on business with Samoan residents, held any interest in Samoan land, or transacted with a licensed Samoan bank without the Registrar's approval.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a consumer micro-SaaS, confirm that all subscription revenue originates exclusively from non-resident customers and is collected through approved offshore payment rails (Paddle, Lemon Squeezy); any Samoan-source revenue forfeits the ICA exemption.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a WST 500 fixed penalty plus WST 50 for each day of continuing default; non-payment of the annual government fee triggers automatic strike-off, a 5-year disqualification of the company name, and reinstatement only by court order with full arrears settled.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory dividend withholding tax under the Income Tax Act 2015 on dividends paid by taxable Samoa companies; 0% withholding tax on dividends, capital distributions, and share buybacks paid by an International Company under the International Companies Act 1987 exemption.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For outbound distributions from a taxable Samoa company, treaty relief requires: (i) application to the Samoa Ministry of Revenue for a Tax Clearance Certificate and Certificate of Residence (Form TC-01), (ii) completion of the relevant DTA claim schedule, and (iii) lodgement of the certified certificate with the paying or receiving tax authority; if the certificate is not produced within 30 days, the 15% statutory withholding is applied. For an IC, no treaty protocol is needed because the distribution is already exempt at source.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory non-resident withholding rates are 15% on IP royalties and 15% on debt interest paid by taxable Samoa residents; treaty-reduced rates (typically 5% to 10%) apply under Samoa's limited DTA network (e.g., Samoa-New Zealand DTA) upon TRC submission; IP royalties and interest paid by an exempt IC to non-residents are outside the scope of Samoan withholding tax entirely.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: WST 1,000,000 aggregate annual cross-border related-party transactions (revenue plus expenses) above which Samoa TP documentation, including a Local File and Master File aligned with OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines, must be contemporaneously maintained and filed with the Samoa Ministry of Revenue upon request; below the threshold an exempt IC must still retain arm's-length pricing evidence for the IC's international credit and payment obligations.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Economic Substance (International Companies) Act 2019 applies to ICs conducting relevant activities, which includes IP holding and cross-border software licensing; a micro-SaaS deriving subscription revenue from overseas customers falls within scope and must demonstrate core income-generating activities (CIGA) in Samoa: locally managed decision-making, qualified staff resident in Samoa, operating premises, and expenditure proportionate to income; a purely passive IP-holder with zero presence is automatically presumed non-compliant and an annual economic substance declaration must be filed with the Registrar together with the annual return.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion / abusive reliance on the IC exemption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the consumer micro-SaaS with Samoan-resident customers (subscription sales to natural persons in Samoa), holding a Samoan bank account without exempt-entity authorisation, or structuring related-party payments to shift any Samoa-source income offshore through undocumented fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Loss of the IC tax exemption, reassessment of derived global income at 27% CIT, monthly late-payment interest, and penalties up to 200% of the tax evaded under the Income Tax Act 2015; additionally a fine up to WST 1,000,000 for breach of the foreign-business licence condition of the International Companies Act 1987.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts will pierce the corporate veil where the IC is used as a sham; directors become jointly and severally liable for unpaid CIT and penalties, are exposed to departure prohibition orders (travel bans) issued by the Samoa Ministry of Revenue, and face imprisonment of up to 7 years for tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Earning subscription and licensing income solely through offshore payment rails (Paddle, Lemon Squeezy) while having no employees, no premises, and no management functions in Samoa; a pure pass-through entity with all development subcontracted overseas and zero CIGA in Samoa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A penalty of WST 250,000 per relevant activity plus WST 25,000 per month of continuing default under the Economic Substance (International Companies) Act 2019; the Registrar may cancel IC registration and revoke the tax exemption, resulting in full retrospective taxation at 27% CIT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false economic substance declarations are personally liable to fines up to WST 1,000,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; veil-piercing applies where the IC is a sham, and a struck-off IC cannot be reinstated without court order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / beneficial ownership and due diligence failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to disclose truthful ultimate beneficial owners to the licensed IC service provider, failing to maintain the protective BO register, or processing consumer SaaS payments without knowing the beneficial owner, in breach of the Samoa AML/CFT Act 2019 and the service provider's KYC obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to WST 300,000 for the company and WST 150,000 for each responsible officer; revocation of the registered agent's licence can void the IC's standing and cause automatic striking-off, and correspondent banks may blacklist the IC, terminating Paddle or Lemon Squeezy payout flow.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face disqualification orders, personal travel bans, and criminal prosecution for money laundering or concealment of the UBO; confiscation of personal assets proceeds under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2007.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Missing the annual return filing date or the annual government fee deadline within 30 days after the incorporation anniversary while subscription revenue continues to accrue offshore through payment rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: WST 500 fixed late penalty plus WST 50 per day of continued default; automatic strike-off after 6 months with assets vesting in the Registrar, and any trading while struck off attracts fines up to WST 100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: After strike-off, directors remain personally liable for debts contracted during the default, cannot reuse the company name for 5 years, and any asset distribution during the strike-off period is a criminal offence carrying imprisonment up to 3 years and personal restitution to creditors.
